about: Every dimension the F/A-18C build uses, with its source (an id in references.json) and where in it. Values are in the source's own units; the build converts. Stations (FS) are inches aft of the fuselage datum, waterlines (WL) inches above it (WL 100 is the fuselage reference line), buttlines (BL) inches from the centreline, positive to starboard. Angles round the fuselage (theta) follow TM-101724 figure 3: looking aft, 0 is the bottom centreline, 180 the top, 90 starboard and 270 port. A fact taken from the old model, as a last resort, names the old model as its source and says why no other source had it; a detail copied from it under the fair-use policy is listed in its manifest entry (air-fa18c.md #2).

length.also: hatp figure 2 (56.00 ft); tp209033 figure 2 (56.0 ft)
length.note: checked to the foot NATOPS gives it in (+-6 in; user, 2026-11-02): with the stabilator tips' 13 in corner rounds where the photos put them (layout.stabilator, layout.stabilator_corner) the model measures 55.76 ft, and the photos' own apex (FS 59.7, 18 photos) and aftmost point (FS 729.8) give 55.84 ft

exhaust.note: nose apex to the engine exhaust plane: the nozzles' exit (layout.nozzle)
exhaust.also: tp3478 PDF page 6 (54.4 ft, nose to exhaust nozzle exit plane, full scale)

spread.note: 37 ft 6 in, without missiles. hatp figure 2 gives the reference span as 37.417 ft

folded.note: 27 ft 6 in. Checked over the folded panels without the fairings under them (layout.wing_fairing, NATOPS 2.6.1.2's position lights 'under the wing at the wingfold hinge'), which ride the outer panel 9 in outboard of the fold line and turn outboard with it, 4.3 in a side: with them the build spans 341.2 in folded. Photos of folded jets (2026-11-07 sweep: f6790603882, f3315245532, f15612089546, the USS Midway Museum's F/A-18A) show each fairing standing out from the folded panel's outboard face just above the hinge, its lens at its front: they fold with the panel, and NATOPS's figure leaves them out. The two folded photos solved (c8355477, c8183843) read the folded panels 2.3-5.6 in outside the build over FS 480-576 (layout.fold: the angle unsettled). Held to 3 in, not 1.5 (user, 2026-11-16): the fold turns about the upper skin's peak over the fold line, where about the chord plane the outer panel's root face swung through the inner panel's, and that stands the folded panels 1.8 in further out each side (332.6 in) on TM-210726's fold line, the way those two photos read them

fins.note: 15 ft 3 in, to the top of the fins
fins.also: tp209033 figure 2 (15.3 ft, on its gear)

canopy.note: 10 ft 6 in, to the top of the closed canopy

leading.note: leading edge of the mean aerodynamic chord (11.52 ft)

apex.also: tp209033 figure 2 (FS 59.82); tm110216 figure 3.1 (FS 59.9); tp3111 figure 7 (FS 60.60)

sections.note: from the LEX-fuselage junction to the LEX leading edge

graph.note: LEX local span on the full-scale jet, read off the graph to about 1 in; runs about 1 in above tm101724's three stations

fence.unit: in, FS in, BL in, deg
fence.where: figure 7, PDF page 33; text PDF page 8
fence.note: the 0.06-scale model's fence, in full-scale inches: normal to the LEX surface at its leading edge, about 25 deg from vertical

hardware.note: the full-scale fence fitted to fleet jets; its lengths differ from tp3111's model fence, so the 2020s photos settle the shape

underside.unit: FS in; edge: the traced section's LEX edge, BL in; heights: [BL, height above the section's keel] in, along the underside from just outboard of its root to just inside its edge
underside.where: figure 5 (PDF page 31), as traced into references/sections.json (views.py) on the scale the build's LEX top takes from it: each section's underside read every 2 in of buttline, both halves of the drawing averaged (they differ by 0.2-2.2 in, the right half higher; the LEX's root and edge heights average them too)
underside.note: the LEX is a wedge: its underside nearly flat, falling 0.9-2.2 in from root to edge, its upper surface falling onto it at the edge. The first inch outboard of its root is the fillet into the fuselage's side, left out. Ahead of FS 253 its thickness shrinks with its span to the apex; behind FS 357 it comes down to the wing (layout.lex underside)

gun.note: the gun port exits, on the upper centreline near FS 122

probe.note: the in-flight refuelling probe doors, upper starboard side

pitot.note: the two production pitot-static probes, lower fuselage

ecm.note: two elliptical ECM antenna covers on the research jet; confirm on the 2020s reference airframe

scale.note: the 0.06-scale wind-tunnel model's three-view: b = 2.245 ft, length 3.360 ft, S = 1.44 ft2, mean chord 0.691 ft

surfaces.about: Surface positions NATOPS gives for each flap setting, in degrees down, and the mechanical limits (limits).

ground.note: HALF or FULL on the ground; AUTO with weight on wheels is 0

fixed.note: GAIN ORIDE with HALF or FULL

check.where: ground checklist, spin recovery mode check
check.note: 33 +/- 1 deg down with the spin recovery mode engaged: the most the flaps travel in NATOPS

differential.note: up to +/-3 deg below 30,000 ft above Mach 0.7

half.note: aileron droop; 0 with the wings unlocked

full.note: aileron droop; 0 with the wings unlocked

trim.note: takeoff trim drives the stabilator to 12 deg nose up

limits.about: Mechanical position and rate limits, deg and deg/s, from tp209033 table 2 (PDF page 16), which states they are the basic F-18A/B's. tm110216 table 6.2 (PDF page 99) gives the HARV's aileron as 25 up and 42 down.

waterline.note: the fuselage reference line corresponds to WL 100.0 on the airplane

buttline.note: BL 0 is the centreline; BL grows to starboard (Y is right of the c.g.)

apex.note: the fuselage reference line (WL 100) is drawn through the nose apex and on aft past the stabilator; tp209033 figure 2 points WL 100 at the stabilator

chord.note: mean aerodynamic chord, projected; tp209033 and hatp give 11.52 ft (138.24 in) as the reference chord

root.note: NACA 65A with a sharp leading edge, at wing station 56.876 (cr201687 table 1: modified NACA 65A, 5.0%)

tip.note: cr201687 table 1 agrees (3.5%); secondary sources' 65A003 is not supported

span.note: span station of the wingtip at the launcher rail, on a sketch; the reference semispan is 224.5 in

lef.note: each inboard leading-edge flap is 36.5% of the total LEF area, each outboard 13.5%; one actuator drives both

areas.note: totals for both sides. cr3608's 1/10-scale model gives 0.19, 0.55 and 0.62 ft2, which scale to 19, 55 and 62. The flaps' 48.4 is not built: their fronts stand on the hinge line the photos show (layout.hinge), which makes them 55.5

exposed.note: reference span of the exposed panels

area.note: theoretical exposed, both sides; tm4772 table 1 gives 88.26 unmodified

toe.note: toe out, as the model table gives it

rudder.note: both rudders. The rudders' outline is the photos' (layout.rudder), 16.3 ft2 both: 6% over this, its hinge line 1.4 in forward of where this area puts it over that span, inside the photos' spread of hinge lines

top.note: the fin tip 11.34 in above the fuselage reference line on the 1/10-scale model. Anchored at the apex, the HATP side view draws it about 4 in higher and its canopy top at WL 163, which this figure also draws

forebody.note: the McDonnell Douglas drawing's forebody height and width, read off the graphs to about 1 in; agrees with tm101724's sections

buttline.note: TLOC: each engine axis 2.33 ft either side of the centreline at the aerodynamic reference centre (FS 458.56), where the figure draws it

angle.note: EPS: the engine axis's angle to the aircraft's x axis in plan. The axes converge aft: hatp figure 2's top view draws the nozzles at BL 19.5 either side, nearly touching, as photo dvids9820758 shows, which 2 deg of convergence from 28 in at FS 458.56 gives (19.3 in at FS 707)

thrust.note: DXTHRS: the thrust point's distance aft of the aerodynamic reference centre (FS 458.56)

inlet.note: hydraulic diameter of the inlet duct entrance

face.note: the engine face's diameter, where each inlet duct ends (layout.inlet duct): the F404-GE-402's, the F/A-18C/D's engine (page 1), the -102 and -103 alike. Its length there, 154 in, from the face at X/D 6.5 (FS 563.1) reaches FS 717, 3.8 in past the nozzles' exit (layout.nozzle, FS 713.3)

canopy.note: how much bigger the two-seat canopy is than the single-seat one; tp209033 figure 2 draws the two-seat jet

gravity.aircraft: HARV phase 1, 60% fuel, clean, gear up
HARV phases 2-3, 60% fuel, clean, gear up
F-18B SRA, 66% fuel, clean, gear up

airfoils.note: NACA 65A basic thickness forms: half-thickness y at chordwise station x, both in percent of chord. Another thickness takes y/t interpolated linearly in t between the tabulated forms (TR-84's own method, by its cross plots); above 5% the 5% ratios hold, which TR-84's 63-series cross plots show moving under 2% between 5% and 6%.

layout.about: Placements no source states, fitted to the NASA three-views with the published planforms (views.py's masks, the side view anchored at the apex on WL 100). Each says what it was fitted to. The photo gate checks them against the reference airframe's photos (photos.json).

wing.where: figure 5, PDF page 31 (traced by views.py), with hatp figure 2's side view for the keel. The anhedral: photos.py's cameras and tips.py (rotating the wing about the junction; deflections fitted, or held at rest in flight) over the ground photo dvids9820799 and the in-flight photos dvids8901347, dvids7487368 and dvids6690145, their cameras solved with the rest (fin tips within 0.3 in)
wing.note: the wing's chord plane at the LEX-wing junction (BL 54.5, FS 404.05): the FS 357 section's LEX tip stands 31 in above its keel, and the keel is at WL 82.5. The anhedral is the photos', the jet parked (the user's choice, 2026-10-30): cr201687's -3 deg (wing.dihedral) leaves the tips' trailing corners about 5 in low in the ground photo (+-2 in or more: its flaps and ailerons droop) and 10 in low in three in-flight photos (8.7-10.3 leaving each out), the difference the wing bending up at 1 g (task: wing flex). Rotating the wing about the junction fits the flight photos a little better than raising it, and the junction itself measures no higher (4 in lower, +-2.3, two photos). The HATP front view draws the outer wing about 10 in higher

flex.unit: BL in, where the bend starts; in, the wingtip's rise at 1 g of lift; [BL in, share of the tip's rise]
flex.where: the rise: tm212871 printed page 17 and figure 12(a), FDMS target 12 (span station 193.8, figure 5) about 1.4 in, and 1.7 in after a roll, in steady level flight against ground rest, taken to the tip by the ground test's shape; the shape: tm210726 figure 16, load case D3, the forward box's measured deflection (1.1, 1.8, 3.1, 5.1, 6.2 and 10.0 in at the stations, 13.6 in at span station 222.1), read off the figure
flex.note: the wing bent up by lift (task: wing flex), as the shape key flex and the bend joints flex_* driven by the load factor of the lift (the drive load: 0 parked, 1 in level flight). Both reports fly the Active Aeroelastic Wing jet, whose wing has the preproduction torsional stiffness, a little softer than a production C's; its targets outboard of the fold carry the fold's free play. The bend starts at the LEX-wing junction (layout.wing's buttline) and takes a cantilever's shape, lift along the span as the chord and stiffness as the chord times the section's depth squared, streamwise sections rigid: outboard of BL 150 it follows the ground test's shape within 0.015 of the tip's rise, inboard it bends 0.05-0.06 less (the test's load and the fuselage's restraint are not flight's). The photo match agrees within its uncertainty: posed at 1 g with the in-flight photos, the wingtips' trailing corners fit best near a 3.5 in rise and the parked photos' wing and fin edges best with none

fold.unit: deg, the outer wing's turn about the fold line from spread
fold.where: the two photos with the wings folded against the sky (c8355477, deck level ahead of the right wing; c8183843, head-on): c8355477's outline fits best at 103 deg and its tip corners at 101, c8183843's corners at 95-99 (its outline keeps too few of its places as the angle changes to settle one); the middle of those readings
fold.note: NATOPS's folded span (27 ft 6 in) holds at any angle past 90 deg, where the panel's foot at the fold line stands outermost, so it cannot fix the angle: the build took the least angle that met it, 90.1 deg. At 98 deg the two photos still read the folded panel inside their outlines, 2.3-5.6 in (painted49), and pull opposite ways: c8355477's fits best at 103, c8183843's places thin out past 94 and read 0 at 83-92. No one angle fits both, so the panel's own shape or the fold line's place is unsettled, not only its angle. Two more folded views (2026-11-08: f3315245532 and f6790603882, from behind, each camera solved alone) read 92.5-95 deg from the panels' trailing tip corners: the readings spread 92-103 deg about 98, left as built under the plan's tolerance. The hinge runs streamwise along the upper skin's peak over the fold line (WL 112.2, 1.76 in above the chord plane): about the chord plane the outer panel's root face swung through the inner panel's from the first 5% of the fold (2026-11-16); on that hinge the sky check reads the folded ailerons 4.5-5.0 in inside both photos' outlines, up from 2.4-3.3, within the range recorded above (2026-11-17)

stabilator.where: figure 2, top view; natops 1.1.2 for the length; the waterline from the in-flight photos dvids8901347, dvids7487368 and dvids6690145 (tips.py, deflections held at rest, the cameras photos.py solved), and held with each photo's deflection fitted (2026-11-20, scratchpad f233, f233b): each photo-side at its own best deflection, the sky check's stabilator bands read -0.54 to +0.02 in at WL 106.8 against +1.0 at the root (FS 600-624) and +0.73 at FS 624-648 at WL 104, though the photo-sides' own best misses favour 104 (median 0.59 in against 0.71, 40 better and 23 worse)
stabilator.note: the root leading edge of the exposed panel (BL 41.6: the 21.6 ft span less the 14.67 ft exposed span). The views from straight above and below (dvids7487365, 7487366, 9820744), each photo's left and right sides averaged to cancel its camera's registration, read the leading edge 0.1 in and the trailing edge 0.05 in from the model's here (sky check); moving the panel 1.8 or 2.9 in aft took them to -0.6 and +1.5, or -0.9 and +2.5. It was first placed for the 56 ft overall length with an 8 in corner round; with the photos' 13 in round (layout.stabilator_corner) the tips' aftmost point falls at FS 729.8, 2.9 in short of it, and the photos' own apex and aftmost point give 55.84 ft (overall.length). WL 106.8: the in-flight photos put the tips' leading corners 6.8 in above where cr3608 figure 3's and tp209033 figure 2's WL 100 had them (at rest 6.3-7.7 leaving each photo out; 4-7.5 with trim free), the root then 3.8 in above the engine axes (layout.nozzle, WL 103); the HATP side view draws them about 10 in higher. The spindle is not published

stabilator_corner.where: the sky check's photo edge places round each stabilator's trailing tip corner, cast onto the posed panel's plane, fitted as the cited tip line and trailing edge joined by a circle tangent to both, the panel's offset free (each photo's registration): 13.25 and 13.25 in (dvids7487365 left and right), 12.0 and 12.25 (dvids9820744), 13.0 and 13.0 (dvids7487366), 12.25 (dvids7487368 right), fitting to 0.13-0.19 in rms (0.52 for the last). The model's own outline through the same fit reads 7.5-8.0 for its 8. Variants with the panel unmoved: the corner's sky check, each photo's sides averaged, read +2.76 in with 8 in and +0.51 with 13 in, the leading and trailing edges unchanged (+0.10, +0.05). HATP figure 2's top view, a small drawing, cuts the corner back about 11 in along the tip, where a 13 in round leaves the tip line visibly (by 0.5 in) about 17 in from the corner
stabilator_corner.note: the radius of the round on each stabilator tip's trailing corner, tangent to the tip and to the trailing edge, 20.5 in from the corner along each; it takes 1.3 ft2 off the 88.0 for both sides (stabilator.area). cr201687's planform, which the build keeps everywhere else, is the theoretical one with sharp corners. Judged by where the traced tip seemed to leave its line it was first put at 8 in: a 13 in circle stays within 0.5 in of its tangent for 3.6 in past the tangent point. The leading corner reads sharp and the leading edge straight within a few degrees of the cited sweep. The corner landmarks stay where the edges' lines meet, as the photos are marked

fin.where: verify/photos.py over photos.json (12 photos solved together): the fin tips' four corners in 6-9 photos (+-1.8 in along, +-0.3 in across); moved 1.5 in forward (2026-10-31): the fin tips' leading corners in 15-16 photos stand 2.0 in forward of the earlier build (+-2.2) and the trailing corners 2.9 in (+-2.4), and the sky check (verify/skyline.py) reads the leading edge 0.6-1.0 in inside the photos' all along it (FS 528-624, 10-14 photos each), about 1.0 in of stations at its sweep: the move lies between the two; moved 1.0 in further forward (2026-11-02): the tips' leading corners in 16-17 photos stood 1.0 in forward of the build (+-1.3) and the trailing corners 2.0 in (+-1.4), the leading edges traced in 13 photos and cast onto each fin's own plane 1.2 in forward all along their height on both fins (no sweep the photos agree on: single photos tilt both ways), and the sky check read the leading edge 0.4 in inside and the aft end 1.0 in outside
fin.note: leading edge at root and tip, on cr201687's planform, sweep and cant: the photos put the tips 8 in further aft and 7 in further outboard than the HATP views were fitted to give (FS 613.6, BL 71.4), the HATP side view's own top trailing corner standing 8.8 in aft of the old fit too; the root lies 95 in down the 20 deg cant from the tip (BL 38.9, on the nacelle's shoulder)

fairing.unit: top: [FS, WL] in, the fairing's upper edge on the fin's outboard face, from where it meets the leading edge to the band's aft end; foot: [FS, BL] in, its lower edge on the nacelle; step: in, how far its upper edge stands off the fin's face; standoff: in, how far its foot stands outboard of the fin's face carried straight down; aft, the plate from the band's aft end to the rudder's lower leading corner: top [FS, WL] in, its upper edge on the fin's face; seam, in, how far it stands in from the band at the band's end; step, in, how far its upper edge stands off the fin's face at its aft end, eased in from the band's; foot, [FS, BL] in, its lower edge on the skin; clear, in, how far forward of the rudder's hinge line it ends
fairing.where: a riveted band along each fin's root on its outboard side, its upper edge the bolt row along the tops of its notches, continued forward as a riveted seam to the leading edge, its foot the lower edge of the root strip where the plain nacelle skin begins; it ends at the seam at the last notch's aft edge (2026-11-06). Marked by a helper in dvids9820801, dvids9820808 (right), dvids9820782, dvids9820788, dvids9820749, dvids7418477 (left) and triangulated as mirrored pairs through the bundle's cameras: each point 4-5 rays over 51-83 deg, the rays within 0.1-0.9 in. The upper edge lies on the build's fin face within 0.3-0.7 in. step and standoff: from straight behind (navy090715N6106R097, the left fin within 1 deg of edge-on, 338 px/m) the outline steps out 9 px at the band's top and stands 16-20 px outboard of the fin's edge carried down, 22-26 px at its lower end. The foot's waterlines, 125.0, 119.2, 120.1 and 121.5 at the four stations, stood 1.0-3.6 in above the build's nacelle shoulder at those buttlines; with the deck's shoulders lifted to the fins' roots (2026-11-20, build.py DECK_LIFT) the skin there reads +0.5, +1.9, +0.5 and -2.4 in against them. The build stands the foot on its own skin. aft (2026-11-16): a riveted plate carries on from the band's end to the rudder's lower leading corner, with only a thin seam step where the band ends and no end face (dvids9393266 left, dvids9820808 right); its upper edge cast through each camera onto the fin, from the band's end (FS 603.4-605.0, WL 128.2-129.3) through FS 609.1-610.8, WL 127.4-128.2 to the hinge line at FS 616.9-617.3, WL 126.3-127.2, 1.6-1.8 in above the rudder's lower edge. Its foot is the fin root's line the photos cast (layout.panels fin_root_fillet_right, its points from FS 601 aft): it draws in from the band's foot (BL 42.3 at FS 601.0) to BL 40.8 at 602.7 and 39.0 at 605.5, then runs close along the fin's face carried down to the skin (BL 38.8-38.3) to FS 615; drawn in over 3 in from the band's own foot instead, the plate covered the line for 3 in behind the band. Its seam step and its stand-off at the rudder's corner are the user's ruling (2026-11-16, as recommended): a 0.2-0.3 in step at the band's end, under 0.5 in at the corner

rudder.unit: span: the rudder's lower and upper edges as fractions of the fin's span from its root chord; hinge: its hinge line as a share of the fin's chord from the leading edge, the same from its lower edge to its top; corner: [FS, WL] in, the hinge line's lower end; its trailing edge is the fin's
rudder.where: the rudder's top edge, hinge line and lower leading corner read at full size in nine fins of eight solved photos (dvids9820808, dvids9820801, dvids8842278, dvids7847398 right; dvids7418477, dvids9393266, dvids7243901 left; dvids8842845 both) and cast through each photo's camera onto the build's fin (2026-11-16). Top, where it meets the hinge line: 0.664-0.671 of the span, mean 0.668 +-0.003 (63.5 +-0.3 in), each photo left out in turn 0.668-0.669; hinge: 0.773-0.807 of the chord fin by fin, each straight from bottom to top within 0.01, mean 0.790 +-0.011, each left out 0.788-0.792; lower leading corner, seven fins (the far fins' hidden behind the nacelle or the stabilator): FS 614.7-619.0, WL 123.5-126.3, 1.1 +-0.9 in above the root chord, mean FS 617.0 +-1.5, each left out 616.7-617.4. The top edge runs along the span's line from the hinge line to the trailing edge, which lies on the fin's (0.986-0.994 of the chord where the rudder stands at rest). navy090715N6106R097, from behind, reads the tops at 0.65-0.68, loosely
rudder.note: replaces 0.42 of the span read off tp209033's sketch, which stood the top 24 in low and the lower leading corner 8 in forward; the photos agree within their spread, no photo standing apart. Its area, 16.3 ft2 both, is 6% over cr201687's 15.4 (fin.rudder), whose hinge line over this span (0.80 of the chord) lies inside the photos' spread

hinge.where: dvids7487365 (straight below, sharp, against clear sky): one straight line, with the hinge fittings and actuator fairings on it, runs along the lower surface of both wings across the flap and the aileron; traced at 16 points (BL 57-225 right, 57-211 left), cast onto the posed wing, it lies at 0.704-0.720 of the chord, rising inboard; the value is the median of the 11 points along the flaps. The aileron's front, which cr201687's aileron area sets (wing.areas, 0.699), stands 0.3-1.0 in ahead of it on both wings; cr201687's flap area would have put the flap's front 4.6-5.0 in behind it
hinge.note: the lower surface's hinge line of the trailing-edge flap and the aileron, as a share of the wing's chord from the leading edge. The flaps' fronts are built on it, which makes them 55.5 ft2 for both sides, where cr201687 table 1 gives 48.4 and cr3608's 1/10-scale model 62; the flaps' area is not built. The traced line is a photo match edge (dvids7487365 hinge_*), which the old flap missed by 4.3-4.4 in. dvids9820744, softer, read the same line 1.2-5.0 in ahead of the old flap front and 3.1-4.2 in behind the aileron's: both now about 3 in off it the same way, its camera's registration

surfaces.where: figure 2 (control surfaces labelled in the top and side views); the flap's outer end and the aileron's inner end by photo match, with tm210726 figure 6
surfaces.note: spans of the hinged surfaces: the leading-edge flaps split at the fold (tp209033 PDF page 17) and run from the LEX-wing junction to the tip; the flap's inner end is read off figure 2's sketch (the rudder's, 0.42 of the fin's span, stood 24 in low: layout.rudder). The flap's outer trailing corner is the photo match's fold_trailing point (BL 152.8 +- 0.8, six marks in five photos), 7 in inboard of the sketch's 160; the gap to the aileron is 3.1 in wide at the trailing edge in dvids9820744. tm210726 figure 6 (to scale within 1%: its two references and the tip agree) draws the load zones on the flap ending at BL 154 and those on the aileron starting at 156. The aileron's inboard 6.5 in lies behind the fold line and folds with the outer panel. The aileron runs to the tip (the sketch drew it ending at BL 220): with it drooped in dvids9820782 and dvids9820788, sky shows directly outboard of its end, under the tip's launcher rail. Each surface's chord fraction follows from its cr201687 area over these spans

gear.unit: FS in for the axle centres; WL in for the axles; in for the track (between the main wheels' centres) and the nose wheels' spacing; legs: main: top, the post's top where it leaves the airframe [FS, WL, BL]; droop, deg the trailing arm hangs in flight below its standing angle; pivot, the trailing arm's pivot boss's middle; brace, the side brace's highest point seen on its axis and its lower bolt's inboard end; link, the planing mechanism's connecting link: a point on its axis, the axis's direction (the right leg's; FS, WL, BL per inch of WL) and the polished rod's two ends; arm: tip, the trailing arm's end where the axle's stub begins [FS, WL, BL]; shock: ends, its top pin, the boss on the post's top casting where it meets the skin, and its eye on the lug on the arm's top [FS, WL, BL]; hidden, in, its white upper cylinder's reach up its line past the pin into the bay; fitting, in: the radius of the yoke's lugs round the pin, their caps 5 in across, and the span across the pin's ends; fittings, in: yoke each arm's thickness, of the shank's forked forward end, pin [the hollow pin's ends' diameter, bore], lug the diameter of the pivot fitting's lug between the yoke's arms, web [its front aft of the pin, depth] the forging joining the arms, socket [aft of the pin, diameter] where it closes round the shank, collar [distance from the pivot, stand off the shank, length] the split collar, tab [share of the length, length, width, height] the small lug on the shank's top, rod the hold-down damper: top [FS, WL] its trunnion pin on the keel's aft face, lug the distance from the pivot of its clevis on the forging's top, diameters [cylinder, piston], cylinder [above its pin, below it], piston its length, end [the rod end's length from the centre of its eye, its eye's diameter]
hook.where: The pivot (2026-11-22) at dvids9820808's own cast onto BL 0, FS 647.5, WL 76.9: the lowered shank's two edges, fitted in the four side views with the hook down (c8203275, f54337945831, f6545328211, navy110715NDE843014) and cast onto BL 0, run 55.1-57.0 deg below level through FS 647.5 at WL 76.9 +-0.6 (c8219137, landing, from the front quarter: 77.1), where the pivot verify/photos.py read before (hook_pivot in dvids9820808 and navy090707N7665E003, FS 649.9 +-2.3, WL 77.6 +-3.5) left the lowered shank's root 3.5 in aft of theirs; its length the 67.9 in from there to the stowed point, the lowered shoe 68.9 away; the hold-down rod's top moved with it. Before: hook_point in navy090707N7665E003 alone on the centreline, FS 713.6 +-2.7, WL 96.3 +-4.0, between the nozzles. Length: 66.4 in to that point; the lowered hook's shoe cast onto BL 0 in dvids9820748 (FS 718.1, WL 59.3: 70.6 in, 15 deg down) and dvids9820749 (718.9, 74.6: 69.1 in, 2.5 deg down), whose shank also casts to the pivot (648.4, 77.5); the point is placed at their mean, 68.7 in, along the stowed direction (16.3 deg up aft). The fitting's cap 5 in across in dvids9820808. Shank, point and fittings (2026-11-16): dvids9877274 (stowed, from behind, solved, 11.9 px/in) shows a round shank about 3.2 in across a third of the way from the pivot, 2.7 mid-way and 2.0-2.3 near the point; dvids9820808 reads its depth 2.3-2.8 (29 px at 0.097 in/px near the pivot); the user's ruling (2026-11-16, as recommended): a round shank tapering from 3.0 to 2.4 in. The 4.4 in width read from navy090707N7665E003 (22 px at 5 px/in) is dropped: that photo's solved camera gives about 2.5 px/in at the hook. The point in dvids9877274: a head about 5.3 in wide with a rounded top and an aft-facing bore about 2 in across, side lugs or bolt heads spanning about 7.6 in, a darker shoe below; US Navy 050124-N-4308O-018 (hook down, close, no solved camera: ratios to the shank only) shows the point as a boss with an aft bore on a flat skid wider than the shank, chamfered at its ends, with side bolts, the boss about 1.8 shank diameters across and as long as it is wide; c8203275 (3 px/in, low confidence) puts the skid about 6-7 in along and 2 in thick. The pivot in dvids9820808: the cap about 5 in across round a hollow pin (its bore 15-20 px, 1.5-1.9 in), the shank's forward end a yoke round it; 050124-N-4308O-018: a box clevis there, a split collar near the shank's top (about one shank diameter aft of the yoke) and a rod from the fuselage down to a bolted lug at the shank's top just aft of the yoke; dvids9820748: a small lug on the shank's top about a third of the way along. Stowed angle (2026-11-05): the sky check's side views read the shank's lower edge at FS 690 0.6-2.0 in under the earlier build's (c61468204 -2.0, dvids8842845 -1.8, dvids2211572 -0.6, level views), which puts the stowed hook 13.6 deg up aft instead of 16.3 and its tip at FS 716.7, WL 93.8 (the same 68.7 in from the pivot), inside navy090707N7665E003's 96.3 +-4.0. Length (2026-11-05): seen from below, the sky check's edges on the shoe's tip near the centreline cast onto its height put it at FS 712.6-714.9 (dvids931513 and 931513b from 81-84 deg below, 714.4-715.0 and 713.6-713.9; dvids7487365 and 9820744 from 63-65 deg, 712.6-712.9 and 712.3-712.5), and dvids7487365, sharp, shows the dark shoe ending at FS 713, read against the solved camera's projected stations, as navy090707N7665E003's mark has it (713.6): the tip is placed at FS 713.5 along the stowed direction, 65.4 in from the pivot, 3.2 in forward of the lowered hook's casts' 68.7 mean. The casts (69.1-70.6 in) and the stowed tip cannot both hold for a straight hook turning about this pivot; the stowed tip, which every view from below shows, is taken, and the lowered hook's reach stays unsettled; lowered (2026-11-06): the shoe's lowest point triangulated from four hook-down photos (f54337945831, f6545328211, c8203275 in flight, c8219137 landing; 4 rays over 69 deg, each within 1.6-3.4 px), 60 deg below the horizontal from the pivot: with the stowed tip 13.6 deg above it, the hook travels 73.7 deg (it had swung an earlier 62, its tip 10 in high and the sky check reading the lowered hook 5.7 in outside over 5 photos). The lowered point stands 68.3 in from the pivot, the stowed tip 65.4: as before, a straight hook about this pivot cannot meet both, and the build turns the hook to the lowered point's direction, its shoe 2.9 in short of it; point and pivot re-read (2026-11-17) at full resolution: navy131008NZG705121 (a Marine F/A-18C, stowed, from behind) and navy080711N3946H116 (an F/A-18C, stowed, from behind and below) show the point as one casting: the shank's end a thin ring round the bore at the top of the flat aft face of a body with flat sides and chamfered top corners, the face about as tall as it is wide, overhanging the shoe, the ring 0.70 of the face's width across and the bore 0.50-0.57 of it, a hex bolt head on its port side and a hex nut on its starboard side about the bore's height, and under the body a shoe wider than the bolts, its shoulders carried out of the body's sides at three quarters of the face's height, rounded below to a U (its rounded end 0.46 of its half-width deep), its sole dished inside a rim worn to bare metal; navy080711N3946H176 (from below) the shank flaring smoothly into the body; f54337945831 (abeam, hook down, 6.4 px/in across the shank) and c8203275 the shoe standing forward of the shank's end below it, its throat face 6 deg below the horizontal with the shank 58 deg below it: it leans 24 deg from square to the shank toward the pivot, and its tip stands 3.8 in from the shank's line. Widths from dvids9877274's solved camera (11.9 px/in across at the point): the body's face 48 px (4.0 in), the bolts' heads 62 px (5.2 in), the shoe's shoulders 84 px (7.0 in); the face white down to 2.4 in below the bore's centre (row 2098 against 2069, 12.1 px/in up), the shoe's shoulders from 1.6 in below (row 2088). The earlier reading's 5.3 in head was the bolts' span and its 7.6 in side lugs the shoe's shoulders: navy131008NZG705121 and navy080711N3946H116 put the bolts' span at 1.48 and the shoulders at 1.93 of the face's width. Finishes: the shank, the forging at the pivot and the point white, chipped (navy131008NZG705121; usmc131002MSO590006 the shoe painted, scratched to bare metal; 050124-N-4308O-018), the bolts plated steel; navy080711N3946H116's Navy jet a bare steel shoe. The pivot: navy090401N2562S004 (hook down, from port below): the yoke a white forging, stained by fluid, its arms round the pin closing aft into a socket with a band where the shank enters, the hold-down damper's polished piston coming down from the skin to a white rod end with a jam nut on a clevis on the forging's top, bolted through; 050124-N-4308O-018 the same white forging and rod end
hook.note: the stowed hook hangs below the aft fuselage from its pivot at the keel's aft end, its shank climbing 13.6 deg aft into the channel between the nacelles, its shoe tucked between the nozzles. The earlier build placed the point at FS 684 from a mark on the place the shank passes into the body's outline in a side view (about 30 in forward of the shoe) and the pivot 9 in forward: a 43 in rod. The hold-down rod is estimated from 050124-N-4308O-018's proportions scaled to the shank (its pin on the keel's aft face 10 in above the pivot, its lug 5 in along the shank, a cylinder and a piston telescoping as the hook lowers): no solved photo sees it. The point's body length (as long as it is wide, 050124-N-4308O-018), its 3.5 in flare, the shoe's reach (its lowest point 5.0 in below the line, between f54337945831's 3.8 and navy080711N3946H116's U about 3 in below the face), its sole's dish (0.3 in deep inside a 0.5 in rim) and its sole standing 0.35 in forward of the aft face, which overhangs it, the bolts' place along the body (0.9 in ahead of the face), the forging's web and socket (from navy090401N2562S004's proportions) are estimated; so are the damper's lengths (its cylinder 2.5 in above its trunnion and 5.8 below, its piston 7.7 in, its rod end 1.6 in), set so it telescopes with the rod end clear of the cylinder stowed and 1.1 in of piston still in it down, and the keel's aft end turning with the hook's sideways swing about the upright through the pin, which no photo shows: with the keel fixed, the yoke's arms swing through its aft end. The point's rounded head (2026-11-20, the user's ruling on #245: the shank as it is, a more rounded head, as the old model's reads): the body's section above the line a half round over its 4.0 in face (top 2.0, dome 2; the photos show a flat-sided face with chamfered top corners, 1.4 in above the line), the shoe leaving the body's sides on a 0.7 in fillet (was 0.4; at most half the shoe's width past the body's, 0.75, or its outline folds back) and every edge of its section rounded 0.9 in (was 0.5), its measured width, reach and lean unchanged; drawn for the look, not measured, and nothing of the old model's geometry taken

petals.unit: outer flaps per nozzle; in, the exit's radius closed (military power); in, the throat's radius closed (military) and open (full reheat); in, the tailpipe's radius where the convergent flaps start; in, the convergent flaps' length; in, the divergent flaps' length; the stepped tabs: their station as a share of the outer flaps' length from the exit, and their step round as a share of a flap's width
petals.where: the count from the three photos (both nozzles of one jet end-on, 12 brackets each; a second jet's 12 trailing-edge gaps; a third's flap tabs 30 deg apart); tm101741 printed page 3 for the nozzle areas, 220 in2 at military power and 348 in2 at full reheat; tm88273 printed page 4 for the 12 primary flaps and 12 seals inside; tm100159 figures 12 and 14 for the exit, calculated R9 24.20 cm and 23.04 cm at military power (test conditions 5 and 6: M 0.9 at 24,000 ft and M 0.4 at 30,000 ft), their mean; tp3531 figure 7 (printed page 120) for the convergent section, the 0.10-scale inner nozzle's 2.640 in bore and 0.834 in flap (its throats, 1.674 and 2.105 in at 35.390 and 18.708 deg, are tm101741's areas); the stepped tabs measured on navy020214N3896H001 (an F404 out of its jet, the nozzle open), each a ratio on one flap: the step 0.24 of the outer flap's length from the exit (0.25 as the image shows it, the near exit end foreshortened less, so +-0.05) and 0.23 of the flap's width round. The divergent flaps' length is not measured: nothing of known size stands at the flaps' depth in the open-nozzle photos
petals.note: the throat's radii are the areas' circles. The closed exit's radius is the gas path's, at the divergent flaps' faces, which the build stands 1.5 in inside the outer flaps (no source gives their thickness): closing turns each flap about its hinge until that face reaches it, the outer lip then about 10.8 in from the axis, as dvids7070877 (from behind, both nozzles closed) shows it, about 10-11 in. tm100159's R9 is GE's spec deck's, the measured jet 5-10% wider (its page 8), and a running jet on the ground at intermediate holds a wider throat (264 in2, tm4538), so a closed nozzle seen low down stands a little more open. The parked photos show the nozzles open; the HARV (tm101724's jet) had its outer flaps removed. The divergent flaps' length is the eye's (no source gives it). The stepped tabs are measured (layout.petals where): each outer flap's aft part steps round by 0.23 of its width 0.24 of its length from the exit, so the seams between flaps make a staircase

Refitted on 2026-11-16 with the side brace's foot's clevis among its members, judged by check.py's crossing test on the build's own meshes (scratchpad fit194b, about 3,200 paths): no path clears both the clevis's lower end, which crosses the open inner door on this path, and the shock's can, which every path clearing the clevis runs about 2 in through the nacelle's lower skin aft of the bay opening (FS 491-500); leaning the foot's bolt or opening the inner door further does not clear it either. This path is kept (user, 2026-11-16), and the clevis's crossing is signed off with it (layout.motion braces). The stowed leg reaches WL 106.1 and BL 41.7, so its bay is deepened to WL 107.4 and out to BL 42.7 (layout.wells); the room-solved pose signed off on 2026-11-13 (109.1 deg about [-0.649, -0.312, 0.694]) missed those hubs by 5-9 in. stowed.unit: nose: deg the nose leg stowed above forward; main (the left leg, the right its mirror): axis [FS, WL, BL] the trunnion's axis, swing deg the leg's turn about it from down to stowed; shrink in the shock absorber's stroke: out in flight over pushed in on the ground, which the shrink link draws it in by as the leg stows (the trailing arm turned up about its pivot from its droop to its standing angle); turn [FS, WL, BL] the axis the axle and wheel turn 90 deg about at the arm's end, with the arm drawn up; trunnion in up the post's axis from where it leaves the airframe

braces.where: the nose drag brace is the actuator the photos show (layout.gear legs nose actuator): its cylinder turns about its pin in the airframe to aim at the web's pin and its rod slides out of it as the leg swings forward, the rod as long as keeping the overlap inside the cylinder at full stretch needs, its inner end 3 in or more short of the cylinder's pin (build.py actuator()). The main side brace folds at its knee, which gear down stands where the photos last see the brace (layout.gear legs main brace's first point): dvids4642471 (VMFA-115, 2018, from inboard and ahead of the left leg) shows the knee's boss there at the bay's edge, the lower half lit from the foot up to it and the upper half going on up into the bay, so the lower half is 18.4 in, not the 14 in of a knee 0.57 of the way up (2026-11-19); the knee's boss 2.4 in across (150 px against the tube's 111 px, its 1.8 in) and the downlock spring 0.8 in across with its coils 0.25 in apart (48 px and 15 px), running from the knee on up into the bay; the structure pin at FS 462.0, WL 80.2, BL 24.2, the upper half 8 in, found by a search of the brace's plane for the fold that keeps the boss and the tubes clearest of the post, the doors, the bay's walls and the duct through the stroke (scratchpad f208/pinfit_near2.py), with the inlet duct's section at FS 460 raised 2.5 in for the room (layout.inlet.duct); the connecting link's pin on its axis at WL 82, 1.4 in off the trunnion's axis, so its ends draw apart little over the swing, and the bell crank, on a bracket off the arm's pivot boss, its pin at WL 56 where the photos lose the rod and its 4 in arm square to the link (6 in put its boss in the shock absorber's can, which the arm's droop brings forward in flight) (an arm along the link, pinned on the boss itself, sits at dead centre and cannot hold the length), turns little; the brace's halves, the link and the crank hinge about axes along the trunnion's, so the leg's swing keeps each in its plane. The link as dvids8678626 shows it (2026-11-15, at the post's 46 px/in, +-0.1 in): a white sleeve 1.15 in across (53 px) down to the polished rod, 0.6 in (28 px), with a lock collar 1.1 in across and 0.5 long at each of the rod's ends (50 and 23 px), and a white rod end 1.0 in (46 px) on down to the crank's pin
braces.note: the rod's reach into the cylinder at full stretch estimated, nothing seeing inside it; the main side brace's structure pin, the boss's length along its pin (2 in) and the spring's length into the bay (5 in), the connecting link's pin and its bell crank's place: no photo shows them, unseen, placed for room. The main side brace's fork at its bolt (2026-11-16): an eye 3.1 in across round the bolt, tapering 3 in up the brace into its tube, either side of the post's lug, the bolt's pin hollow at its outer end and with a round head at its inner; each cheek's 0.4 in thickness, which no photo shows edge on, is estimated. The pin through the fork reads 17.5 deg off the trunnion's axis in dvids8678626 (it runs 19.7 deg below the photo's horizontal from its hollow end to its head, the axis 2.3 deg; taken square to the brace its end face would read 0.50 against the photo's 0.5, the axis's 0.38), and dvids8678629's soft view of its end, about 25 deg (+-10) from the photo's horizontal, sits between the two (-17 and -1); the build keeps the bolt along the trunnion's axis, which its brace's planar linkage turns about. What reads face on in dvids8678629 is the slot between the cheeks above the bolt. Under the fork the foot turns in a clevis on the post across the bolt, a universal joint's second pin (dvids8678626 from outboard, 46.7 px/in, read relative to the fork's centre, the camera there 2.4 in off): two lugs off the post 1.6-2.6 and 4.2-5.3 in down a bolt through the fork's middle, a spool 2.8 in across between them, and under the lower lug the bolt's castellated nut 2.8 in across (5.5-6.6 in down) and its rounded end 1.7 across to 7.8 in. The bolt runs 18.6 deg aft of the photo's vertical through the pin's centre, the fork's block's bottom, the spool's middle and the nut's; taken square to the pin as the photo measures it, it is (FS 0.284, WL -0.957, BL 0.066) down on the right leg, 18 deg off the post; no second photo sees it, so its lean across the sight line and the lugs' width round it (the spool's and 0.3 in) are estimated (user, 2026-11-16: built from the one view). On the main leg's path (layout.motion stowed main) its lower end, from the lower lug down the bolt to the end, passes through the open inner door and the skin at the bay's edge at gear 0.375-0.45: no path clears it without running the shock's can through the skin, and the foot's depth is the one view's least certain reading (user, 2026-11-16: kept, a known crossing). The knee's boss and spring clear the post, the doors and the bay's roof by about 0.4 in through the stroke on the search's sampled surfaces (2026-11-19), the knee photographed and the pin placed to make room for them.
braces.unit: link: the side braces' diameter, in (their tubes' measured 1.8); overlap: how far the nose drag brace's rod reaches into its cylinder at full stretch, in; side: the main side brace's structure pin [FS, WL, BL] (the right leg's), boss the knee's boss [diameter, length along its pin], spring the downlock spring [diameter, pitch of its coils, its length from the boss up the upper half], in, and its fitting: the fork at its bolt, its length from the bolt up the brace to where it meets the tube, its eye's diameter round the bolt and each cheek's thickness, either side of the post's lug, in; and foot: the clevis under the fork, bolt the direction its bolt runs down through the fork's middle [FS, WL, BL] on the right leg, lugs each lug's [top, bottom] down that bolt from the fork's middle, spool its diameter, nut [across flats, top, bottom], end [diameter, bottom], in; connecting: the connecting link's structure pin and the bell crank's pin, WL in on its axis, the crank's arm from its pivot to that pin, in; sleeve, rod and end, the link's diameters down its length, in, and collar its lock collars' [diameter, length], in

swing.note: the hook's sideways travel each way estimated (NATOPS 2.10.5 gives no figure), and its time from centre to either stop estimated: 40 deg/s both ways, toward the pull of the wire the hook holds and back to centre once the wire lets go (no source gives the liquid spring's rate)

hook.note: the stroke time estimated, within NATOPS's maxima: "Hook extends in 3 seconds maximum and retracts in 6 seconds maximum" (NATOPS III-10-13)

band.unit: centre: [FS, WL] on the centreline, the belly between the nacelles; floor: [FS, BL, WL] the band's edge, the main gear inner doors' inboard edges to FS 557 and the band's flat out to BL 18 at FS 599; both smoothed over 6-8 in through the measurements, 12-20 in apart; measured: the points they were smoothed through (centre: [FS, WL, BL, what]; floor: [FS, BL, WL], the triangulated corners) and the tolerance, in, the check holds the skin to them; reach: BL in, out to which the outline under the nacelles takes the band's line, meeting the nacelles' own there; fade: FS in, the stations over which the band eases in from the forebody and out to the tail
band.where: 2026-11-12, a helper over the belly photos (scratchpad tunnelsolve): every point has rays from ahead-below (f33825978748, f7390543136, f15265384461) and from behind-below (navy040107N3799S002, dvids7487365), 75-90 deg apart, 2 px moving each 0.3-0.5 in. measured centre: three drains (FS 481, 497, 513), the louvred grille's corners (FS 520, 534, at BL 4.6), the small holes either side of the exhaust hole (559, BL 3.8), the exhaust hole (565), the keel's front pin (582), a seam across at FS 599 (BL 6-18, flat at WL 79.4-79.9); FS 619 is the keel's measured bottom (layout.keel, WL 75.1) plus its lit side, 4.4 in tall in dvids9820808. measured floor: its corners triangulated (FS 450.6, 499.3, 533.4: left 76.32, right 75.13, the left taken, the right's two forward marks disagreeing by 1.8 in) and the plate's front corners (FS 556.8, BL 7, WL 76.4); between them the seam traced in navy040107N3799S002 and f7390543136 and cast onto the corners' line, the two 0-2 in apart; FS 404 is the forebody's keel (layout.belly). Smoothed: the knots lie within 0.2 in of the drains, grille and holes, 0.6 in above the keel's front pin (a highlight on a cylinder) and 0.5 in below the FS 599 seam, rounding the rise between them
band.note: there is no tunnel between the nacelles: the HATP fit hollowed the belly 6-8 in deeper (WL 84-85 at FS 480-560, 86 at BL 6 at FS 600), where the photos put a nearly flat band level with the doors' inboard edges, crowned 0.5-1.2 in on the centreline. Ahead of FS 481 the SUU-62 (to FS 445) and the centreline tank's tail (to about FS 490) hide the centreline in every view from below, so the band's line there is interpolated from the forebody's keel (layout.belly, FS 404) to the first drain, eased in over the fade; behind FS 619, where the keel's sides are the last seen, it eases back to the fuselage's own line by the nozzles; behind FS 599 the band carries on 0.8 in above the nacelles' lowest line (layout.nacelle line and aft), flat out to BL 18, as the photos have it at FS 599-619 (the keel's sides put it at WL 79.5 at FS 619, the line 79.7): held level there instead it dipped 1.5 in under the nacelles at FS 650, and turned up between knots 28 in apart it creased the skin 3.8 deg at FS 620
